Working out whether 192.168.1.130 is on the same network as 192.168.1.73/26 should take a few seconds. Guess wrong and you end up with a VPN range that swallows your LAN, or a firewall rule that matches far more than you meant. This guide shows how CIDR notation maps to bits, how to find network and broadcast addresses by hand, how to carve a /24 into subnets for a home lab, and how to check what your Linux hosts are configured with.
An IPv4 address is a 32-bit number. Dotted-quad notation splits it into four 8-bit octets and writes each one in decimal, so every octet runs from 0 to 255.
192      .168      .1        .73
11000000  10101000  00000001  01001001

The prefix length after the slash says how many of those 32 bits, counted from the left, identify the network. The remaining bits id…

Quick answer: When an agent adds a "small helper" that already exists elsewhere in the repo, you don't just have a duplicate file. You now have two functions that look identical today but will drift apart the first time someone fixes a bug in one of them. Treat the discovery of an existing utility as a hard stop: reuse it, or deliberately consolidate, never silently fork it.
I found the pattern on a routine review of a checkout change. The agent had introduced formatMoneyCents() in a new pricing.ts. It was well written, it had a unit test, and the feature worked. The problem was that packages/currency/src/format.ts already exported formatCurrency(), which did the same job with one extra responsibility: it applied the rounding rules that finance had signed off on after a real incident with …

articles.description:
On October 19, Go shipped two security releases: 1.27.3 and 1.26.10. The fix touches a single package, crypto/x509. I rebuilt one of my Go services on the same Docker image as before. Go's own scanner still found the flaw.
TL;DR: the eMudhra fix is a list of eight banned keys, written into the code of crypto/x509. That list is compiled into your binary. Updating the base image or the system certificates does not add it. You have to rebuild with Go 1.27.3 or 1.26.10, then redeploy. If your Dockerfile still builds with Go 1.25, rebuilding changes nothing: that version gets no more fixes.
Versions and source status: snapshot as of October 31, 2026. Check the latest fixes before deploying.
This article is for Go developers and for teams that ship Go services in containers.
eMudhra is a certifi…
articles.title: The eMudhra fix lives in your Go binary, not in your Docker image

AI coding assistants like Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot are remarkably fast—but without strict boundaries, they invent missing business logic, assume requirements, and break existing codebase rules.
In this deep-dive article and video walkthrough, we cover Spec-Driven Development (SDD) using two of the most powerful workflows in modern AI engineering: OpenSpec and Superpowers.

articles.description:
Q9. A user sees “This account is currently not available” at a terminal, or the GUI returns to the login prompt. How do you troubleshoot it?


Start by inspecting the account rather than editing /etc/passwd directly:
getent passwd nerds

The final field is the user's login shell. If it is /sbin/nologin or /usr/sbin/nologin, an interactive login normally prints a “not available” message. If it is /bin/false, the shell exits immediately and may simply return to a login prompt. These are not necessarily errors: service accounts are often deliberately prevented from logging in interactively.
For a real user account that should have terminal access, change the shell with usermod:
sudo usermod -s /bin/bash nerds
getent passwd nerds

You can also use chsh -s /bin/bash nerds where permitted. Avoid…
